speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions you are concerned about, including their size, shape, and color?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of a non-healing, crusty lesion on your penis and a similar one on your finger, along with your smoking history, is highly concerning for malignancy. Have you noticed any bleeding, pain, or changes in the size or shape of these lesions since they first appeared?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP) to assess for anemia or systemic infection.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, night sweats, or malaise. No other similar lesions elsewhere on the body. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your anxiety, but we must confirm the nature of these lesions before proceeding; given the description of non-healing, crusty areas on your penis and finger combined with your heavy smoking history, I am highly suspicious of Squamous Cell Carcinoma. Please perform a biopsy on both lesions immediately to confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the penis and digit.
